title: Openings
note: One opening card per origin: it fires in year 1 and says where you are, who you report to and what you do, so the first year starts with context. Written to the plain-English rule: what is happening, why it matters to you, then the joke.

events.title: Four Months In
events.body: You came back from your overseas degree four months ago and were posted to the {ministry} as an Assistant Director. Your reporting officer is {senior}, {senior.aTitle}. Today {senior} hands you your first real job: a paper for the Minister, due in two weeks, on why a scheme isn't reaching the people it was built for. The officers who run its counters have done it for years, and nobody has asked them. A scholar's first paper gets read closely.

choices.text: Spend the first week at the counters.
choices.outcome: You spend five mornings behind the counters, and the paper says what the counter staff have known for years, with numbers. {senior} sends it up unchanged. The Minister's office asks who wrote it, and why it reads as if the writer had been there.

choices.text: Ask a scholar from your year, now in the Minister's office, what the Minister wants.
choices.outcome: Your friend in the Minister's office tells you what the Minister likes to read, and in what order. The paper lands well and comes back with a tick. {senior}, who wasn't asked, notices that nobody asked.

choices.text: Write it from the files, and hand it in early.
choices.outcome: The files are thorough, and so is your paper: correct, and a day early. It goes up with a tick and comes back with no comment, which for a first paper is a comment.

events.title: Eight Months In
events.body: You've been a Management Executive at the {ministry} for eight months, mostly drafting replies to letters from the public. Your reporting officer is {senior}, {senior.aTitle}. {peer}, who joined the same week as you, already gets sent to meetings you don't. Your first appraisal is in four months.

choices.outcome: {senior} gives you a briefing note for a Deputy Secretary, due Friday. It's harder than anything you've done. It goes in on time, with one mistake that {senior} catches before anyone upstairs sees it.

choices.text: Ask {peer} how to get into those meetings.
choices.outcome: {peer} says you just ask to sit in. So you ask. The meetings are mostly about scheduling other meetings, but people upstairs now know your face.

choices.text: Keep your head down and clear the letters.
choices.outcome: You clear a hundred and forty replies by December, each one checked twice. Nobody upstairs counts them. {senior} does, and starts sending you the letters nobody else wants to answer.
